headline: A One Hundred Fifty Eight Dollar Apology, Written Mostly In Overs
paragraphs: Sixty three games went under the knife, eighteen walked away untouched, and forty five of them produced tickets. Seventy one of them, ten dollars each, seven hundred ten in total exposure. The model walked in expecting to win 61.4 percent of those and won 37.7 percent, which is the kind of gap you normally only see between a resume and a reference check. Final damage was 158.34 dollars and an ROI of negative 22.3 percent.

Spreads did the heavy lifting on the way down, going 9-18-2 and dropping 98.19 with a straight face. Totals chipped in a 10-16 and 69.10 while projecting 67.2 percent confidence, the single funniest number in the file. Moneylines, the market nobody brags about, finished 7-9 and still cleared 8.95 for a positive 5.6 percent, meaning the one segment that lost more bets than it won was the only one that made money. The published top five went 2-3 for a loss of 11.82 against an expected 72.1 percent, so the stuff we put our name on performed roughly like the stuff we did not.

Two plays deserve the spotlight. Air Force and Army closed 24 to 21, forty five points against an Over 43.5 the model loved at 84 percent, and it cashed 9.09 by the width of a field goal, which we will be calling vision. The reverse was East Carolina 20, South Florida 17, where Over 39.5 came in at 78 percent and died three points short. Fifty three of the week's lines moved and exactly four moved toward us, 7.5 percent, a number the market should frame. Season now sits at 187-243-12 across 442 plays, down 586.04 at negative 13.3 percent through seven real weeks. There is a hindsight week floating around at 40-25-1 and plus 110.47, graded after the fact, which counts for precisely nothing and feels exactly as good as it sounds.
